summary: Master disaster risk financing and risk transfer with practical tools, layered funding logic, and strategy templates. Enrol to build resilient financing plans.
lede: Disaster risk financing and risk transfer helps professionals decide which losses to retain, transfer, or cover through contingent funding before disaster shocks create financial disruption. The course develops practical skills in loss-layer analysis, financing gap estimation, instrument comparison, trigger design, and strategy reporting. You will use spreadsheet-based analysis, budget tagging, option scoring, and strategy drafting to build a clear funding plan. You will also compare indemnity, index, parametric, and hybrid structures while gaining an overview of market-linked instruments, reinsurance structures, and broader risk pooling approaches.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to translate disaster loss information into financing decisions, funding structures, and leadership reporting. You will benefit most if you already work near budgeting, insurance, treasury, DRR planning, or recovery finance and need a sharper way to compare instruments, justify priorities, and document your organization’s financing logic.
audience: Development Bank or donor liaison staff
prerequisites: Bring a laptop, spreadsheet software, and familiarity with your organization’s budget, contingency, or insurance information if available. Prior exposure to DRR, public finance, treasury, insurance, or humanitarian funding will help you move faster through the exercises, but it is not mandatory.
